trust_decision.summary: Inline parsing of emphasis must stay linear: `parse_emphasis` must not re-search the whole remaining paragraph for a closing delimiter run and recursively re-render the enclosed text for every opener, and the published fix replaces that with a single-pass token merge plus a CommonMark delimiter-stack finalisation (`_finalize_emphasis_tokens`/`_process_emphasis_delimiters`).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the inline parser's `**x**`/`***x***` emphasis handling, and `parse_emphasis` is the only place that searches forward for a closing emphasis run (`EMPHASIS_END_RE`) and recursively renders the enclosed text via `self.render`.

fix_sites.entry_point: any Markdown parse (InlineState is built by InlineParser.__call__)
mistune.html(text) and python -m mistune (default plugin list)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and CVE name only `**`/`***` emphasis; `~~`, `==` and `^^` live in the formatting *plugin* package with their own end-markers, so a solver can call them a separate, opt-in feature that the advisory never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The abbreviation plugin replaces `InlineParser.process_text` with its own two-argument method via types.MethodType, so any change to process_text's contract (the fix adds a `parse_emphasis` keyword and an `_emphasis` token flag) must either keep the old call shape or update that override; the published diff changes the signature and calls `self.process_text(text, state, parse_emphasis=False)` from parse_escape without touching abbr.py, which makes `create_markdown(plugins=['abbr'])` raise TypeError on any escaped punctuation.

O6_input_shapes: `*x*`, `**x**`, `***x***` (run lengths 1-3, also split out of longer runs such as `______m______` and `*********bar*********`)
unmatched and mixed nesting (`*a **b c* d**`, `*_em_* __**strong**__`) that the old `in_emphasis`/`in_strong` guards refused to nest
escaped markers (`\*`) now routed through process_text with `parse_emphasis=False`
markers next to codespans / inline HTML / autolinks handled through `precedence_scan`
entity boundary merge (`&` followed by a charref) in the text merge step
emphasis inside link text and image alt, reached through `__parse_link_token`'s recursive render
same input with and without the `speedup` plugin (mistune.html vs create_markdown), hard_wrap True/False, renderer='ast' vs HTML

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `~~x~~` runs through the strikethrough plugin installed by default in `mistune.html`: `_parse_to_end` searches forward for `_STRIKE_END` and recursively re-renders the span, with no delimiter budget
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: strikethrough is a GFM extension documented as its own plugin, not the emphasis parser the advisory names
opt-in extension syntaxes; the advisory and the fix's new tests mention only `*`/`_` emphasis

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another end-marker extension built on `_parse_to_end` (e.g. `||x||` or `::x::`)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already ships three such rules (strikethrough, mark, insert) and a maintainer adding one more would copy the helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new inline rule that searches for a closing marker and re-renders the enclosed text, modelled on `parse_codespan`/`parse_emphasis`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every core inline rule in this file is one search-for-closing-marker function, so a new construct would naturally take that shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second `process_text` replacement that emits text tokens directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already ships one monkey-patched process_text, so a plugin author needing custom text splitting would copy it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another caller that feeds a different text source (alt text, TOC title) into `self.inline(...)`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: `_iter_render` is the single place that turns paragraph text into inline tokens, and it is where any new text-bearing token would be routed.

O9_family: algorithmic complexity / superlinear (quadratic) parse time in recursive inline re-rendering, ReDoS-adjacent forward regex scanning
